$comment: The surface the accessibility gate scans. Keep it in step with the visual specs under
e2e/visual/: a route that is worth photographing is a route that is worth scanning, and a
route in neither list is a route nobody is checking.
Every path here has to exist in `src/routeTree.gen.ts`. The list was aspirational once - it
named the whole intended product - and the scan answered with 146 `route-unavailable` errors
per run, which made the gate fail on every commit without auditing a single page. A gate that
is red by definition is a gate nobody reads, and it hid two real violations for three days.
So a route lands here in the change that builds it, not before.
It also has to be complete in the other direction, which is the half that rots quietly:
/categories, /import, /payees, /reset-password and /settings all existed and were never
scanned. When you add a route, add it here.
`access` says what the scanner has to do before the page will render:
public   - no session; the page is served to anyone.
form     - no session, and the page IS an authentication form, so the enhanced
accessible-authentication probe (SC 3.3.9) runs against it.
session  - the scanner signs the demo account in first.
Dynamic segments ($accountId, $transactionId, $budgetId, $seriesId, $goalId, $payeeId,
$ruleId, $batchId) are absent on purpose: their ids come from the seed and would pin
this file to the fixture. The e2e suite covers them with ids it looked up at run time.
/accounts/groups is absent for a different reason than the rest: it does not exist, but it
also does not 404. `/accounts/$accountId` matches `groups` as an id, so the route answered
HTTP 500 where every other missing path answered 404. That turned out not to be about this
path at all - seven of the eight dynamic-segment screens answer 500 for an id that names no
row - and it is now issue #16 rather than a note here.
